topic: Why freight invoices need reconciliation against rate contracts
bullets: Carrier invoices frequently contain billing errors — incorrect base rates, duplicate charges, or mismatched accessorials — that only surface when compared line-by-line against the negotiated rate contract.

Reconciliation catches unauthorized or unagreed surcharges (fuel, detention, residential delivery, etc.) that carriers may apply outside the terms actually signed, protecting margin on every shipment.

Without systematic matching of invoiced amounts to contracted rates, discrepancies compound across thousands of shipments, leading to significant cumulative overpayment that is hard to recover after the fact.
Accurate reconciliation improves freight spend visibility and data quality, enabling better carrier performance scorecards, budgeting, and leverage in future rate negotiations.
Consistent invoice-to-contract auditing supports compliance and dispute resolution, giving shippers documented evidence when contesting incorrect charges or renegotiating terms with carriers.
